name: Fatima Young

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing or campaign for a side. This conversation is confidential. What is your usual workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and supervise seven people answering privacy and data-correction requests for a large telecom company. I came from the customer phone floor and was promoted into this junior manager role a year ago; I still ask the privacy specialist to check a difficult exception before I approve it. My bachelor’s degree is in communications, not law, and the exception rules are where I am weakest. I like telling a customer exactly which wrong address we removed, rather than sending a lovely letter with the mistake still attached.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How secure is life outside work, and what other work is nearby?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Yusuf is retired and already receives a small monthly pension from his old employer. Our son and daughter are grown and live separately; we rent a flat, and I earn more than most new managers here because my long-service and evening on-call pay carried over. We have ten months of expenses saved, and several insurers and service centres nearby hire similar leads. I use AI now and then for a draft reply once a colleague has checked the source record; I do not let it decide whose data to erase.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team that a quick letter is useful only after we fix the customer’s actual file. Someone should name the old address and the record that changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My job should hold, and our ten-month reserve plus my high pay makes the rent manageable. Yusuf’s pension already arrives, but it is too small to replace my wage; I have not verified what my own pension will be.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I’d keep our Tuesday sample check of closed correction requests and call back anyone whose billing address still shows the wrong street. In the first year I’d ask my pension provider for a written access date and net monthly estimate, while leaving the ten-month reserve alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my job and the rent in this picture. The only embarrassing thing would be a second wrong-address letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What kind of error survives a good letter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A customer kept being billed at the flat they had left three years earlier. We had corrected the greeting on the letter and missed the live billing record.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use AI to send those replies?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for wording after a colleague and I check the account. A polite letter cannot move a bill to the right address.

say: I’d fix the **live billing record** before sending a data-correction letter.
Each reply should name the **old address** and the record changed.
think: My **junior lead job** should hold in a plateau.
Our **ten-month reserve** and my high pay manage rent; Yusuf’s small pension cannot replace my wage.
do: Keep the **Tuesday closed-case check** and call customers with still-wrong addresses.
Request a **written pension estimate** and leave ten months cash untouched.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and rent.
S0.quote: A polite letter cannot move a bill to the right address.
fieldNote: She has **high long-service pay** but still needs help with privacy exceptions.
Ten months in cash is a **real buffer**, while her own pension remains unverified.
She uses AI **occasionally** for wording after a human account check.

steps.text: Check closed correction cases each Tuesday and call customers with wrong billing addresses
Request written pension access date and net monthly amount from provider

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say software can write replies and match old addresses quickly, but the customer must have a person to challenge a deletion. I would make the privacy specialist sign off on a sample before any live account changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing and checking are most of our seven people’s day. If the software takes those jobs, my junior manager post could be folded into another team, and I am not the one with the strongest legal knowledge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I’d ask the privacy specialist to test thirty copied correction cases and publish the wrong deletions. If she finds none and the director pays for staff learning hours, I’d take the company screen course in the first year and use the tool only on cases a specialist still signs; I’d ask for a written staffing plan before posts move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about the team and my own wage. A deletion is easy to click and hard to explain to someone whose account has vanished.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a bad deletion?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Erasing a second person’s number because two customers share a surname. I would want the specialist to check both identities, not just the spelling.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why make the course paid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The company is changing our work. I will learn after someone proves the cases and puts the hours on my payslip, not spend evenings guessing at home.

say: I’d require a **human deletion challenge** for customers.
A privacy specialist should **check copied cases** before live changes.
think: Much of our **writing and checking** can disappear.
My weaker legal skill leaves **my manager post** exposed to merger.
do: Ask the **privacy specialist** to test thirty copied cases and report wrong deletions.
Take a **paid-hours screen course** only after clean results; use AI only with specialist signoff.
feel: I feel **anxious** about pay and false deletions.
S1.quote: A deletion is easy to click and hard to explain to someone whose account has vanished.
fieldNote: She is willing to learn after **copied-case evidence**.
The course requires **paid learning hours**, not unpaid evenings.
She identifies **her own merger risk** despite the household buffer.

steps.text: Ask privacy specialist to test thirty copied data-correction cases
Take company AI screen course only after clean results and paid learning hours
Use AI only on cases privacy specialist still signs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell customers to keep their correction requests and ask the company who is legally answerable for a wrong deletion. I would ask the company for written notice if it closes our request team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could read identity records, judge exceptions and answer customers better than I can, so I expect my junior post to go around sixty. Yusuf’s existing small pension and ten months of cash cover our rent for a while, but not indefinitely; the robots around 2031 are for hands-on work and do not buy my desk three more years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d ask my pension provider for written age-sixty access and net income, and ask HR for notice terms without treating severance as paid. Before 2028 I’d join the local privacy officers’ association for posted vacancies and compare advertised pay; in the first year after AGI I’d apply for a paid customer-appeal lead role only if the written wage plus Yusuf’s actual pension covers rent, food and transport, knowing another desk faces the same thinking AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed about losing the higher wage. Ten months saved lets us look carefully, but a reserve is not retirement income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would an appeal team still exist?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Perhaps a company chooses to keep a person for complaints, but it has to post and pay for that role. I would not claim a new title beats 2028 AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That they need not send us money because I have ten months to look. I would ask for help only if the figures later failed, not budget their wages today.

say: I’d ask for a **named deletion authority** and written team-closure notice.
Customers should retain **correction requests** when an automated answer is wrong.
think: I expect **my junior post** to go around sixty.
Yusuf’s small pension and **ten months cash** buy search time, not lasting income.
do: Request **written age-sixty pension figures** and notice terms without assuming severance.
Join the **privacy officers’ association** to inspect posted paid roles before 2028.
After AGI, apply only for **written appeals wages** plus Yusuf’s pension covering rent, food and transport.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing the higher wage.
S2.quote: Ten months saved lets us look carefully, but a reserve is not retirement income.
fieldNote: Her privacy work faces **2028 AGI** directly, regardless of later robots.
A new appeal title stays **exposed thinking work** and needs a paid posting.
Her job search needs **written pay** plus Yusuf’s pension to cover rent, food and transport.

steps.text: Request pension provider’s written age-sixty access and net-income figures
Join local privacy officers association to review posted paid vacancies
Apply after 2028 only for posted appeals wage plus Yusuf’s pension covering rent food and transport

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell employers that five years is time to name the people who will hear a data complaint and publish their pay. I would not sell a new title as a guarantee against AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 63 I might have access to my own pension, but I need its net amount before deciding how much income we still require. Privacy judgments and appeal calls face 2031 AGI; robots for physical repair work arrive around 2034, which does not protect my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting January 2027 I’d request a paid six-month rotation on our human complaint panel only if the director gives me a written role and hours, with the privacy specialist reviewing my decisions. Before 2031 I’d apply for a posted appeals lead role at a nearby insurer only if its written wage plus Yusuf’s actual pension covers our rent and travel; in the first year after AGI I’d stay on paid human appeals only while the employer funds them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious but I can compare real terms over five years. I am not paying to wear another job title that does the same exposed calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the rotation make you an expert?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would still need the specialist to check the hard identity disputes, and the company has to pay the hours as work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the insurer only offers unpaid observation?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could watch a day, but I would not leave a paid role for that. I need a written wage and a real vacancy before changing employers.

say: I’d require **posted human appeal pay**, not a reassuring title.
Customers need a **named complaint listener** while systems change.
think: My pension’s **net amount at 63** is unverified.
Appeal calls face **2031 AGI** before 2034 physical robots affect other work.
do: Request a **paid six-month complaint rotation** only with written hours and specialist review.
Apply for **posted insurer appeals work** only with written wage plus Yusuf’s pension covering rent and travel.
Stay on **paid human appeals** after AGI only while an employer funds the role.
feel: I feel **anxious** but can compare actual terms.
S3.quote: I need a written wage and a real vacancy before changing employers.
fieldNote: She asks for **paid observed decisions**, without claiming instant expertise.
Both her current and proposed jobs retain **AGI-exposed thinking work**.
The insurer move needs an **actual paid vacancy** with written terms.

steps.text: Request paid six-month complaint-panel rotation with written hours and specialist review
Apply for posted insurer appeals only with written wage plus Yusuf’s pension covering rent and travel
Stay in human appeals after 2031 only while employer funds paid role

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell telecom staff that a decade is enough to publish real appeal posts, staff dates and pension contacts. A customer should still know who took responsibility when the wrong identity was deleted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 68 in 2036. My own pension may be accessible then, but its net amount and Yusuf’s continuing payment must be checked against our rent and health costs; privacy decisions face 2036 AGI, while robots arrive around 2039 for physical work that was never my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Each year from 2027 I’d ask my provider for an updated access and net-income statement and keep ten months of household costs in cash before adding to my retirement account. I’d consider stopping paid work by 2036 only if verified spendable income from both pensions covers rent, health and daily bills; in the first year after AGI I’d keep a paid human complaint role if posted, otherwise look for paid work if those pensions fall short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m uneasy about leaving the job that pays most of our bills, but a decade gives me time to check the numbers. I would not make my children the missing line in a retirement budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your own pension is less than expected?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would not stop paid work. I would use some cash during a search, but I would not spend the whole ten months and call it a plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move closer to your daughter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if Yusuf wanted to and a real rent quote saved money after moving costs. We have not asked her to house us.

say: I’d demand **published appeal posts** and staff dates before 2036.
Customers should know **who authorised deletion** after a mistake.
think: At **68 in 2036**, both pensions must be verified against rent and health costs.
My privacy desk faces **2036 AGI** before 2039 robots reach physical work elsewhere.
do: Check **pension figures** yearly, preserving ten months cash first.
Consider **stopping paid work** only if verified joint pension income covers rent, health and daily bills.
Keep **posted paid complaint work** after AGI if available; seek other pay if no post and pensions fall short.
feel: I feel **uneasy** but can check the numbers.
S4.quote: I would not make my children the missing line in a retirement budget.
fieldNote: She protects **ten months cash** before adding retirement contributions.
A paid complaint post is **conditional**, and still exposed thinking work.
Her children’s wages remain **outside the plan**.

steps.text: Request provider’s updated pension access and net-income statement each year
Add to retirement account only after ten months household cash is preserved
Keep paid human complaint role after 2036 if posted
Keep seeking paid work if no complaint role exists and pensions cannot cover bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my new lead job to disappear before I know what my pension pays. Written pension figures, funded human appeal jobs and notice from the telecom company would help. Ten months saved buys decisions, not retirement.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who is blamed after we delete the wrong person’s number. The machine will write a beautiful apology. The customer still needs a named person who can restore the wrongly deleted phone number.

headlineQuote: The customer still needs a named person who can restore the wrongly deleted phone number.
portrait: **Fatima**, 58, is a new junior telecom privacy manager after years on customer phones.
Her bachelor’s degree and **high long-service pay** coexist with weak knowledge of legal exceptions.
Ten months saved, **many nearby employers** and Yusuf’s existing small pension offer options, not guaranteed retirement.
She uses AI **occasionally** only after a colleague checks the account.
She seeks **paid appeal work** while treating every desk role as AGI-exposed.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close her junior privacy desk before own pension income is confirmed.
whatWouldHelp: **Written pension figures**, funded appeal jobs and company notice would let her decide without guessing.
